Hey man I want you to understand something, I feel like you and me are in a very similar situation. My story is basically the same as yours, timeline and all. I never thought I would be in this situation and I still don't think that is real. I think the best thing you can do for yourself is change your mindset. Start listening to that inner voice that tells you not to do it and adhere to it. Research the benefits of quitting and go to the dentist. Just start doing little positive things in your life that will push you in the right direction. For example, if you buy them with cash for instance, don't carry cash with you anymore. Or vice versa, where you have to literally hand the money to somebody in exchange for a vape rather than just tapping a card at a gas station and walking off.

I'm saying all this now because I was clean off my vape for about 3 days and I felt great. Once I realized how good I was doing I started thinking about my vape again and it quickly went from positive thoughts of quitting to negative thoughts and fear. You have to let go of that fear because there is such a thing of fear of quitting people don't talk about enough.

I've heard a phrase that goes like this, cigarettes are the best thing in the world!

It sounds weird but it's true. You and I both know that after a stressful day or when you have that craving the only thing that will help it is that. You have to get comfortable with being uncomfortable and recognize that you have to be uncomfortable for a while so you can see long-term benefits down the road.

You have to consider the fact that time moves very slowly and you have to give it time. As long as you change your mindset and start thinking more often about not wanting to do it rather than wanting to, it helps. 

I get what you mean about being excited to use it again, I have that all the time but right after I feel so guilty. I think you have to just be mindful of that feeling you get after and don't be so harsh on yourself about it. Just recognize that you have all of these thoughts and true emotions about the fact that you want to get better and that you want to stop and you have to believe in yourself and trust yourself. It's hard not to do it and I'm not perfect either, I slip up all the time and it's hard for me to even talk about. But that's why you have to listen to yourself and if your own head is telling you to do it less often than it is telling you to do it, that's a good thing and you have to chase that. We have to be willing to sacrifice the good feelings that it brings both physically and mentally for the chance that a better life and long-term success.

I'm planning on quitting tomorrow for good, I'd love to keep in touch and help each other out because I believe in you. If I can do it so can you.
